identity: What are they, you ask?  If I knew, I'd be afraid to say.  They aren't like other places.  They don't just exist.  Something put them there, piece by piece.  A workshop of unknown purpose.  But also, not like any of that.  Honestly, not really sure if they exist before we pass by, or through them, anyway.  Anything we say about them is basically waxing religiously - maybe they can't be explained.

entries.developer_comments: ~ Description of compact bionic module 'Bionic Treads (Cyberframe 1a)'
identity: Sturdy treads for replacing legs and feet on an Exodii Cyberframe.  They are in fact two side-by-size triangular mechanisms, split in the middle, and independently operated by telescoping knees, to facilitate lifting one tread at a time for carefully passing over obstacles, or climbing stairs or ladders.  One's former ankles and associated anatomy will be integrated into the servomotors.  Unlike bipedal human legs, these move faster over most terrain, but will severely hinder travel over obstacles and through water.  They are immune to temperature and pain and don't bleed.  While they are highly resistant to damage, their external moving parts are less well protected than a standard bionic leg with similar plate thickness.  Due to their size and heft, a heavy-duty 1a-style Cyberframe is necessary for operation.

entries.developer_comments: ~ Description of compact bionic module 'Bionic Left Leg (Cyberframe 1b)'
identity: A bionic left leg and foot fit for an Exodii Cyberframe.  These bionics mimic the dynamics of normal human limbs, but are immune to temperature and pain, don't bleed, and are modestly more sturdy.
